title: Finitely presented kernels on locally Noetherian schemes
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $M$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], and $N$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For every morphism $\varphi:M\to N$, its categorical kernel is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, proof: Noetherian affine finite-module argument; the general kernel form is proved in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.QuasicoherentKernel, lines 284-310

proof.text: Apply the already proved source theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_kernel with the same X, M, N and morphism. The source proof first proves the kernel quasi-coherent using exact localization on affine opens. On each affine open V of X, restrict to Spec Gamma(X,V). The sections of the source module M are finite, because M has local finite presentations and finite generation descends from a finite basic-open cover. Kernel sections inject into these source sections. Gamma(X,V) is Noetherian, so this submodule is finite. Over a Noetherian ring a finite module has a finite presentation; the affine tilde/global-sections isomorphism transports it to a finite sheaf presentation. Gluing these presentations over the affine open cover proves finite presentation of the kernel. This node records the existing closed declaration rather than introducing another Lean theorem.
